chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The rash, immoral oath leaves homes desolate.'

key_terms.الْيَمِينُ الصَّبْرُ الْفَاجِرَةُ: The rash immoral oath — an oath sworn falsely or to wrongfully seize another's property
key_terms.بَلَاقِعَ: Desolate, emptied of inhabitants and prosperity; plural of balqa' meaning barren, empty land

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about false oaths and their consequences?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a hadith from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warning against the immoral or false oath (al-yamin al-sabr al-fajira). This type of oath — sworn falsely, recklessly, or to usurp the rights of others — was understood by early Islamic scholars as a major sin that brings divine punishment, including the destruction of one's household and the loss of prosperity. The phrase 'leaves homes desolate' (tadu'l-diyar balaqi') was a vivid idiom in classical Arabic signifying the complete ruination of family life.
